name: Roth IRA Funded by Kids' Earned Income

advisor.summary: A child with earned income can fund a Roth IRA up to the lesser of compensation or the annual limit — $7,500 for 2026 per Notice 2025-67 — and §408A imposes no minimum age; compensation is the only gate, and the family payroll supplies it. Because the wages already fall within the child's standard deduction, the Roth's after-tax character costs nothing, while qualified distributions under §408A(d) emerge tax-free after the five-year clock and age 59½ — a compounding runway measured in half-centuries. The statute tests compensation, not traceable dollars, so a parent can gift the contribution cash within the §2503(b) annual exclusion while the child keeps the paycheck. The account is held as a custodial Roth until majority. The strategy stands or falls with the payroll beneath it — the wage file is the foundation — and the account passes to the child's control at majority whether the family is ready or not.
mechanics: The ceiling is the lesser of the child's includible compensation or $7,500 (2026) — the §219(b) dollar limit as incorporated by §408A. W-2 wages from the family business qualify even though an under-18 child of the parent owes no FICA on them.
§408A sets no minimum age; providers require a custodial (guardian) Roth IRA for minors, with a parent as custodian and control passing at the state age of majority.

Funding-source flexibility: the statute tests compensation, not the cash trail. A parent may gift the contribution amount — comfortably within the §2503(b) $19,000 annual exclusion (2026) — while the child keeps or spends the actual paycheck.

Qualified distributions under §408A(d) — the five-taxable-year clock plus age 59½, death, disability, or the first-home carve-out — are entirely tax-free, and contribution basis remains withdrawable at any time without tax or penalty.

The Roth wrapper also completes the kiddie-tax picture: growth inside the IRA never surfaces as current unearned income — exactly where the kiddie-tax sequencing wants the first $7,500 of wages to sit.

authority.note: The Roth IRA statute — no minimum age, contributions capped at compensation, and tax-free qualified distributions under §408A(d).
The contribution dollar limit — $7,500 for 2026 — carried into Roth IRAs through §408A(c).
The $19,000 annual gift exclusion (2026) that lets a parent supply the contribution cash without gift-tax consequence.
Sets the 2026 IRA contribution limit at $7,500.

requirements: Bona fide earned income for the child at least equal to the contribution — the family payroll file carries this burden.
A custodial Roth IRA at a provider that accepts minor accounts, with a parent or guardian as custodian.
Contributions made by the return due date and reconciled each year against the child's W-2.
Family acceptance that the account becomes the child's outright at the age of majority.
risks: The leading exposure is inherited, not native: if the underlying wages fail exam as not bona fide — the unsubstantiated-family-wage theory of cases like Denman v. Commissioner, 48 T.C. 439 (1967) — the compensation supporting the Roth collapses with them.
Contributions above the child's actual compensation are excess contributions that draw a 6% annual excise until corrected — the W-2 reconciliation is not optional.
Control passes at majority: a young adult can drain the account, with tax and penalty reaching only the earnings — governance is a family matter the plan should anticipate.
Withdrawals during college count as income in aid formulas even though retirement assets themselves are excluded — time any early access around FAFSA years.
stateNotes: Missouri conforms through the federal-AGI starting point (RSMo §143.121): qualified Roth distributions excluded federally never reach the Missouri return.
No PTET interaction — the contribution and growth sit entirely on the child's side; the deductible wages that create the compensation belong to the hire-children strategy's PTET story.
Missouri-specific: custodial accounts under Missouri's transfers-to-minors law generally vest control at 21, giving the family a few more years of custodianship than age-18 states allow.
reviewChecklist: Child's W-2 compensation meets or exceeds the planned contribution, documented before funding.
Custodial account titled correctly, parent as custodian, and the provider's minor-account requirements satisfied.
Contribution logged against the W-2 in the permanent file, with the April deadline on the calendar.
Family briefed in writing that the account passes to the child's control at majority.

client.teaser: A simple yearly move that can grow into a large tax-free nest egg for your child.
client.headline: Turn your kids' paychecks into decades of tax-free growth
plainEnglish: Once your child earns real wages, they can have a Roth IRA — one of the best deals in the tax code. They can put in up to $7,500 a year (2026), or their total wages if less. The money grows for decades. In retirement, it all comes out tax-free.

It gets better. Your child does not have to give up their paycheck. The rule only asks that they earned at least as much as goes in. So you can gift the contribution money, and your child keeps what they earned.
Time does the heavy lifting. Money invested at 12 or 15 has half a century to grow. A few early years of saving, left alone, can become a very large tax-free sum.
client.analogy: It is like planting a tree in your child's yard instead of yours — same seed and soil, but theirs gets fifty growing seasons instead of fifteen.
benefits: Up to $7,500 a year (2026) for each working child
All the growth comes out tax-free in retirement
You can gift the contribution money while the child keeps the paycheck
The original contributions stay reachable if truly needed
steps: WE confirm your child's wages for the year — that sets the contribution cap.
WE help you open a custodial Roth IRA with the right provider.
YOU fund it any time up to the April tax deadline.
WE log it against the W-2 each year, then repeat.
clientCommitments: Keep the payroll behind the contributions real and well documented
Plan for the account becoming your child's to control in adulthood

annualMaintenance: Reconcile each child's contribution against the W-2 annually
Calendar the April funding deadline and confirm receipt with the provider
Revisit the investment mix and the control-at-majority plan as children grow
deliverables: Custodial Roth IRA setup checklist with provider selection
Annual contribution log tied to each child's W-2
One-page family memo on gifting the contribution and control at majority
